title: Be mindful of Allah
hookLine: be mindful of Allah and He will protect you, the pens have been lifted and the pages dried (Nawawi 19, Ibn Abbas)
tomorrow: the hadith says this line came from earlier prophets. what is it?

lines: YOUNG MAN, I'LL TEACH YOU SOME WORDS.
cards: Waiting is its own job. A test result, an offer, an answer from someone who matters. You refresh the page.
You ask a friend whether it'll be fine, then another friend. Each yes helps for about ten minutes. Then the loop starts again.

One day a boy, Abdullah ibn Abbas, was behind the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, and the Prophet turned and said: young man, I'll teach you some words. They land right in the middle of a refresh loop.

teach.b: From Sunan al-Tirmidhi, in paraphrase: be mindful of Allah, and He will protect you. Be mindful of Allah, and you'll find Him in front of you.
When you ask, ask Allah; when you seek help, seek it from Allah. If the whole community gathered to help you, they could help only with what Allah had already written for you.
If they gathered to harm you, they could harm only with what was already written. The pens have been lifted, and the pages have dried. Mindful here is ihfaz: keep, guard, look after.
Keep Allah's limits and His rights, and He keeps you. That's the exchange, and it runs both ways. And notice where Allah is found: in front of you.
Not behind, checking up. Ahead, already there when you arrive. For a week of waiting, look at the middle.
The hadith doesn't forbid talking it through with a friend. It turns the deepest asking, the three-in-the-morning kind, toward one place. The friends can't settle it.
The refresh button can't. The pages have dried. Some hear that as heavy.
Many readers hear it as rest: whatever the crowd does, it can't add to what's written or take it away.
Do your part, keep His limits, and put the asking where the hadith puts it.

how: Many Muslims memorize this hadith in Arabic, and some recite its lines in hard seasons; it often frames du'a, asking Allah directly, alongside ordinary effort.

games.q: what does “be mindful of allah” mean?
o: keep a written record of every sin
keep God's limits, and God keeps you
worry about God's anger all day long

games.q: the words for the boy — tap the pairs.

s: the hadith promises nothing hard will ever happen to you
it says no one can harm or help except with what was written, and that you'll find Allah in front of you.
the words were taught to Ibn Abbas when he was young
the Prophet calls him 'young man' and says: I'll teach you some words.
'the pages have dried' means effort is pointless
it comes after 'be mindful of Allah': keep His limits, and He keeps you.

games.q: your friend says: if the pages have dried, why study for finals at all? what fits the hadith?
o: be mindful and do your part; what's written is a rest, not an excuse.
she's right: effort can't change what's written, so relax.
the pages only cover big life events, not small things like exams.
games.why: the hadith opens with 'be mindful of Allah': keep, guard, act. the dried pages are where the worry goes, not the work.

practice: If you pray, ask Allah for one thing in your own words, quietly and out loud, and then let the sit hold it instead of your phone.
If not, say the thing you're waiting on out loud once, plainly, and let the quiet carry it for a while. No need to fill the silence afterward.

wordCard.voice: Be mindful of Allah: ihfaz Allah, keep Him, guard His limits, wherever you are. The promise follows straight after: He will protect you.

orig.note: Arabic: be mindful of Allah; literally keep or guard Allah: His limits and His rights.

carryVoice: Carry this: he will protect you, and the dried pages can be a place to rest. Hadith nineteen, kept.

sources.ref: al-Nawawi, al-Arba'in, hadith 19; Sunan al-Tirmidhi 2516 (Ibn Abbas)
Musnad Ahmad (the longer version of the Ibn Abbas report)
